Abstract
Linguistic uses
This article explores the linguistic uses in the play (John Okello’s Sacrifice). The linguistic elements encompass all the fundamental contents used in literary works. The use of language is considered one of the artistic aspects of a literary work, and art contains all the essential components employed to create a literary piece, such as themes, characters, structure, style, and title. In the aspect of language use, critics examine these features—expressions, metaphors, foreign languages, and so on—depending on the critic's objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the drama Sacrifice by director John Okello (2015). The play was written by the Tanzanian author Emmanuel Mbujo. It is a play about the revolution of the Zanzibar government that took place in 1964. Here, the researcher relied on analyzing the use of language in this literary work. Literature is a branch of art that uses spoken language or text to convey a message to society. In order for the intended message to reach the community, it is important for authors to use language creatively in conveying the message to the audience. Emmanuel Mbogo, who resides in mainland Tanzania, presents a drama about the people of Zanzibar (Unguja and Pemba). The expressions given to all the characters in this work correspond to the large percentage of the islands’ population. A language is assigned to each character to suit their role. All the elements used may have carried different intentions, but unfortunately the researcher did not utilize them. The elements of language used aimed to conceptualize the various themes in this drama. Certainly, the foundations of structuralist theory have been considered regarding the use of language in the literary work of this drama.

“Art as Technique” states that for a writer to effectively convey their emotions in literature, it is necessary for those emotions to be constructed in a way that presents novelty to the readers or listeners by utilizing elements of language use (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006). Elements of language use include sayings, figures of speech, imagery, and the use of foreign or indigenous languages that are distinct from the literary work itself. He adds by saying that the innovation of one period is different from the innovation of another period. This means that innovation in literary works must constantly change depending on the audience, subject, context, and time, which prevents the literary work from becoming routine and instead gives it renewed vitality each time it is engaged. Shklovisky emphasizes the concept of innovation by stating that it is not about changing the meaning but rather about the manner or way of expressing something. Introduction  
The use of language is one of the aspects found in the external structure of a literary work, that is, its form. Form encompasses all the essential elements used to shape a literary work, such as setting, characters, structure, style, and the title of the work/anthology, among others. In examining the use of language, critics focus on these elements: expressions, figures of speech, register, foreign languages, etc., depending on the critic’s objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the play *John Okello’s Sacrifice* (2015). This play was written by Emmanuel Mbogo, a literary writer from Tanzania. It is a play that discusses the Zanzibar Revolution, which took place in 1964. The theory of Formalism will guide our discussion. This theory is primarily focused on analyzing the use of language in literary works. Proponents of this theory believe that every literary work employs this approach, as it deals with a fundamental aspect of this branch of art—language, which is the main pillar of literature. In this play, we will identify various elements of language use, guided by the theory of Formalism. 1.1 The Theory of Formalism  
Schmitz (2007) and Carter (2006) have outlined several ideas of formalist theorists as follows: distinguishing between the use of ordinary language and literary language, they believed and emphasized that the concept of innovation or novelty is the main function of art, and they preferred literary criticism to have a scientific orientation; thus, they sought to establish scientific approaches in literature.  
According to the ideas of the formalists, all literary works utilize this theory because a work cannot be considered literary if it does not possess artistic qualities. These artistic qualities involve the construction of language elements that demonstrate the novelty of the work. Therefore, anyone who critiques any literary work based on the theory of Formalism will inevitably have to confront the issue of "novelty"—that is, the features that construct the use of language are unavoidable. The theory of Formalism is among the theories that analyze and explain the use of language in the disciplines of literature and linguistics. This theory originated from activists in two academic circles in Russia: on the one hand, the linguists of the Moscow Linguistics Circle, and on the other, the Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), both aiming to bring revolutions to linguistics and literary criticism (Schmitz, 2007). In conclusion, the theory of Formalism has greatly contributed to the advancement and development of literary criticism. This contribution stems from the concept of innovation or novelty in literary works, the challenges and various debates it has sparked, which have generated diverse knowledge and ideas within the field of literature, as well as the emergence of other theories such as the theory of Modernism. 1.2 The Use of Language in the Play “John Okello’s Sacrifice”  
1.2.1 Simile  
This is a figure of speech that connects two or more things that share a resemblance. The words most commonly used in this figure of speech include: like, as, similar to, such as, among others. In our selected play, this figure of speech appears in many places. Our author Emmanuel Mbogo has made an effort to use every scene according to the dialogues of his characters. In literature, habitualization can occur if the reader or listener perceives a literary work as ordinary and fails to distinguish it from a non-literary (ordinary) work. This results from hearing or reading the work repeatedly. These are words used to emphasize or stress a particular issue. This technique is most evident in the genre of poetry, although it also appears in other genres (Mulokozi 1999). Repetition can appear through the recurrence of a word, rhythm, refrain, or rhyme. In the selected play, John Okello's Sacrifice, this figure of speech has been used. The author has used the following repetitions;
ASHURA: “Today! “Today!” Today at what time… (p.14)
This is a figure of speech used to attribute human actions to non-human entities, giving an inanimate thing the ability to act as a human does. On page six of the selected play, the character RASHID is used to illustrate this figure of personification. Rashid says,
“Is it that I have no mother, that the baobab tree split, and I was born?” (p.6)
Repetition appears in the use of the word ‘today’ in the statement by the character Ashura. This character uses the word to convey emphasis. He wants his companion to specify exactly at what time today he will finish what he is talking about, since today has many hours. 1.2.6 Semantics  
The baobab is a plant. The way plants reproduce is different from how human beings are born. In this statement by RASHID, this plant is given the attribute of giving birth like a human being. This personification has been used to provoke reflection among the colonizers who were oppressing the inhabitants of Zanzibar, urging them to also respect these Black people who were born like other human beings. Mulokozi (1996) states that sayings are short expressions that carry deep meaning within them. In Swahili oral literature, it is claimed that sayings are the result of long life experiences that the elders went through, which is why they often appear to be true whenever they are quoted. In this genre, there are various subgenres such as proverbs, riddles, idioms, and sayings. Proverbs have been used in this selected play. Similarly, on page 3 the author says, “A history that clutched the sunflower or the rose.” The ability to grasp or hold something is possessed by human beings. Human beings grasp things with their hands. In this statement, the author endows history with human abilities, suggesting that it holds, preserves, and safeguards the most valuable things. Sunflowers and roses have been used to reflect good and beautiful things that are appealing in society. RAMADHANI: …Unity is strength and division is weakness (p.10)  
1.2.3 Irony or Sarcasm  
OKELLO: Whatever has a beginning, has an end (p.17)  
RASHIDI: …It is just a chicken’s prayer that does not scare the hawk… (p.17)  
In this figure of speech, the words used have a meaning completely different from the intended meaning. It requires the audience to think deeply in order to discern the intended meaning. The author has also used this figure of speech in this selected play. For example,  
OKELLO: A donkey’s gratitude is a kick. (p.67)
OKELLO: …all three of them have the speed of a tortoise…(p.10)
Patience eats the rotten. (p.68)
The three people referred to here by the character Okello have had their level of performance greatly diminished. It has been reduced so much that it can be compared to the pace of a tortoise, which is known to be extremely slow, in words that cannot be uttered. Indeed, this is irony or sarcasm directed at the intended recipients of this statement. They are being reminded to do things more quickly. 1.2.4 Satire  
This is a figure of speech characterized by intense derision (Senkoro 1981). The words that are heard are completely different from the intended meaning. One character, BIBI, has been used by the author to represent this figure of speech in the selected play.  
BIBI: ...Has the God you worship become your uncle?... This proverb, "Unity is strength and division is weakness," is used to encourage unity among members of the community. It emphasizes that people should stick together in whatever they set out to do. The author uses this proverb through the character Okello as he encourages his fellow youths to go to war in order to stage a revolution and ultimately attain true freedom in their land. The last two proverbs, "A donkey’s gratitude is a kick" and "Patience ends up eating what is spoiled," reflect the regret experienced by the main character of this play, John Okello. This main character made a significant contribution to the liberation of various countries in Africa (including Zanzibar), but was not remembered anywhere. Every time he completed a liberation struggle, he was expelled and ended up in prison. The author has used the technique of irony, stating the proverb in reverse; instead of saying “Patience ends up eating what is ripe,” he wrote “Patience ends up eating what is spoiled.” All this was to express the sorrow of this character, Okello. 1.2.7 Idioms  
The character BIBI poses a question to people who appear to worship God every day, yet their actions are filled with oppression and severe injustice. The deeds they commit do not reflect the teachings of Almighty God. They persecute people, slaves, and anyone else who crosses their path who does not share their skin color. This question is indeed satire directed at those who appear to fear God while committing evil deeds. The author says, God is not to be mocked, deceived, or manipulated. These are brief statements that are used by society to emphasize the truth of a particular matter. “Sanaa kama Mbinu” inasema kwamba ili mwandishi aweze kuwasilisha hisia zake kikamilifu katika fasihi, ni muhimu hisia hizo zijengwe kwa njia inayowaletea wasomaji au wasikilizaji jambo jipya kwa kutumia vipengele vya matumizi ya lugha (Schmitz, 2007; Carter, 2006). Vipengele vya matumizi ya lugha ni pamoja na misemo, tamathali za semi, taswira, na matumizi ya lugha za kigeni au asili ambazo ni tofauti na kazi yenyewe ya fasihi. Anaongeza kwa kusema kwamba ubunifu wa kipindi kimoja ni tofauti na ubunifu wa kipindi kingine. Hii inamaanisha kwamba ubunifu katika kazi za fasihi lazima ubadilike daima kulingana na hadhira, mada, muktadha, na wakati, jambo ambalo huzuia kazi ya fasihi isiwe ya kurudiarudia na badala yake huiwekea uhai mpya kila inaposhughulikiwa. Shklovisky anasisitiza dhana ya uvumbuzi kwa kusema kwamba si kuhusu kubadilisha maana bali ni kuhusu namna au njia ya kueleza kitu. Utangulizi  
Matumizi ya lugha ni mojawapo ya vipengele vinavyopatikana katika muundo wa nje wa kazi ya fasihi, yaani, umbo lake. Umbo linajumuisha vipengele vyote muhimu vinavyotumika kuunda kazi ya fasihi, kama vile mandhari, wahusika, muundo, mtindo, na kichwa cha kazi/antholojia, miongoni mwa vingine. Katika kuchunguza matumizi ya lugha, wakosoaji huzingatia vipengele hivi: misemo, tamathali za usemi, rejista, lugha za kigeni, n.k., kulingana na lengo la mkosoaji. Katika makala hii, tunachunguza matumizi ya lugha katika tamthilia ya *Sadaka ya John Okello* (2015). Tamthilia hii iliandikwa na Emmanuel Mbogo, mwandishi wa fasihi kutoka Tanzania. Ni tamthilia inayozungumzia Mapinduzi ya Zanzibar, yaliyotokea mwaka 1964. Nadharia ya Fomalizimu itaongoza majadiliano yetu. Nadharia hii inajikita hasa katika kuchambua matumizi ya lugha katika kazi za fasihi. Wafuasi wa nadharia hii wanaamini kwamba kila kazi ya fasihi hutumia mtazamo huu, kwani inahusu kipengele muhimu cha tawi hili la sanaa—lugha, ambayo ndiyo nguzo kuu ya fasihi. Katika tamthilia hii, tutatambua vipengele mbalimbali vya matumizi ya lugha, tukiongozwa na nadharia ya Fomalizimu. 1.1 Nadharia ya Ufomalisti  
Schmitz (2007) na Carter (2006) wametoa maelezo ya mawazo mbalimbali ya wanadharia wa ufomalisti kama ifuatavyo: kwa kutofautisha kati ya matumizi ya lugha ya kawaida na lugha ya kisanaa, waliamini na kusisitiza kwamba dhana ya ubunifu au ubishara ndiyo kazi kuu ya sanaa, na walipendelea ukosoaji wa fasihi uwe na mwelekeo wa kisayansi; hivyo, walijitahidi kuweka mbinu za kisayansi katika fasihi.  
Kulingana na mawazo ya wanafalsafa wa ufomalisti, kazi zote za fasihi zinatumia nadharia hii kwa sababu kazi haiwezi kuchukuliwa kuwa ya kifasihi ikiwa haina sifa za kisanaa. Sifa hizi za kisanaa zinahusisha uundaji wa vipengele vya lugha vinavyoonyesha ubishara wa kazi. Kwa hiyo, yeyote anayekosoa kazi yoyote ya fasihi kwa mujibu wa nadharia ya Ufomalisti atakabiliana lazima na suala la "ubishara"—yani, sifa zinazojenga matumizi ya lugha haziwezi kuepukwa. Nadharia ya Ufomalisti ni miongoni mwa nadharia zinazochambua na kuelezea matumizi ya lugha katika taaluma za fasihi na isimu. Nadharia hii imetokana na wanaharakati kutoka mitaa miwili ya kitaaluma nchini Urusi: kwa upande mmoja, wanaisimu wa Moscow Linguistics Circle, na kwa upande mwingine, Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), zote zikiwa na lengo la kuzua mapinduzi katika isimu na ukosoaji wa fasihi (Schmitz, 2007). Kwa kumalizia, nadharia ya Urasmi imechangia sana katika maendeleo na ukuaji wa ukosoaji wa fasihi. Mchango huu unatokana na dhana ya ubunifu au ujanja katika kazi za fasihi, changamoto na mijadala mbalimbali iliyochochea, ambayo imesababisha uwepo wa maarifa na mawazo tofauti ndani ya taaluma ya fasihi, pamoja na kuibuka kwa nadharia nyingine kama vile nadharia ya Usasa. 1.2 Matumizi ya Lugha katika Tamthilia ya “Sadaka ya John Okello”  
1.2.1 Tashbihi  
Hii ni tamathali ya usemi inayounganisha vitu viwili au zaidi vinavyofanana. Maneno yanayotumika sana katika tamathali hii ni: kama, mithili ya, sawa na, mfano wa, miongoni mwa mengine. Katika tamthilia yetu tuliyochagua, tamathali hii ya usemi inapatikana katika maeneo mengi. Mwandishi wetu Emmanuel Mbogo amejitahidi kutumia kila tukio kulingana na mazungumzo ya wahusika wake. Mafano yafuatayo yanaonekana:
“…Uhuru wa Zanzibar unanukia kama manukato ya Pemba…” (uk.1)
Wengi wa wanaharakati hawa walikuwa vijana waliowafahamu na walizoeana, kwani waliweza kujadili pamoja huku wakikubaliana na kutofautiana juu ya baadhi ya mawazo. Walikuwa na motisha na hamasa ya kuanzisha maarifa ya kitaaluma kwa njia yoyote ile, ikiwemo kupitia mijadala. Katika mijadala yao, walijitambulisha kama waumini wa ufomali (formalist) wenye lengo la kuleta mapinduzi katika uwanja wa elimu. Waliweza pia kufanya maandamano katika miji ya St. Petersburg na Moscow kabla ya mapinduzi ya 1917. Kwa sababu ya juhudi za wanaharakati hawa, waliweza kufichua nyanja mbalimbali za utamaduni wa Kirusi kama vile muziki, sanaa, fasihi, na isimu. Katika kipindi cha machafuko na vita vya wenyewe kwa wenyewe, wanafomali walipiga hatua katika kudai haki zao, lakini walizuiwa na wakomunisti, ambao walidai kuwa walikuwa wanatenda kinyume na misingi ya uhalisia wa kijamaa. Wanafomali walijaribu kuelezea itikadi zao, lakini hawakufanikiwa, na mwaka 1930 hii ilisababisha kuvunjwa kwa kundi la wanafomali nchini Urusi. Licha ya kuvunjwa huko, mawazo yao yaliendelezwa na baadhi ya wafuasi wa umbo maalum kama Victor Shklovsky, Roman Jakobson, na wengine katika uwanja wa fasihi na wasomi wengine nje ya Urusi. “Kama nahodha wa meli!” (uk.4)  
“Kama rubani wa ndege!” (uk.4)  
“Kama kamanda wa jeshi” (uk.4)  
Katika kauli zilizotolewa kwa wahusika hawa, tashbihi “kama” inaonekana. Katika sehemu ya kwanza, uhuru wa Zanzibar unalinganishwa na manukato ya Pemba. Hakuna shaka kwamba wenyeji wa Zanzibar walikuwa wakitarajia kwa hamu uhuru kutoka kwa wakoloni; ilipoanza kuonekana dalili kwamba wanaweza kuupata, waliufananisha na harufu ya manukato ya Pemba, ambayo inachukuliwa kuwa kivutio na wakaazi wa huko.

Waformalist walitambulisha dhana mbili kuu katika fasihi: ya kwanza ni ile ya mazoea, na ya pili ni ya kutozoeleka. Kulingana na Carter (2006), dhana ya mazoea hutokea pale jambo linapotumiwa mara kwa mara hadi linakuwa la kiotomatiki. Katika fasihi, mazoea yanaweza kutokea iwapo msomaji au msikilizaji ataona kazi ya kifasihi kuwa ya kawaida na kushindwa kuitofautisha na kazi isiyo ya kifasihi (ya kawaida). Hii hutokana na kusikia au kusoma kazi hiyo mara kwa mara. Kulingana na dhana hii ya kuzoea, Shklovsky alianzisha dhana nyingine—ubunifu au upekee wa kazi za fasihi—katika makala yake katika JOHS Vol.20 No. Kebehi, kama vile mtu anavyoweza kuonyesha kwa mjomba wake mwenyewe. 1.2.5 Marudio/Shada  
Katika kisiwa cha Unguja. Pia katika uk. Mwandishi amemlinganisha Sultan Jamshid na mambo mbalimbali, kama vile nahodha wa meli, rubani wa ndege, na kamanda wa jeshi. Neno "kama" limetumika kufanya linganisho hili katika tamthilia Sadaka ya John Okello. Hizi ni maneno yanayotumika kusisitiza au kutoa mkazo juu ya suala fulani. Mbinu hii inaonekana zaidi katika aina ya ushairi, ingawa pia inaonekana katika aina nyingine (Mulokozi 1999). Kurudiarudia kunaweza kuonekana kupitia kurejea kwa neno, mdundo, kwaya, au vina. Katika tamthilia iliyochaguliwa, Sadaka ya John Okello, tamathali hii ya usemi imetumika. Mwandishi ametumia marudio yafuatayo;
ASHURA: "Leo! "Leo!" Leo saa ngapi... (uk.14)
Hii ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kutoa matendo ya kibinadamu kwa vitu visivyo na uhai, ikivipa kitu kisicho na uhai uwezo wa kutenda kama mwanadamu. Ukurasa wa sita wa tamthilia iliyochaguliwa, mhusika RASHID anatumika kuonyesha mfano huu wa uhuishaji. Rashid anasema,
"Je, ni kwamba sina mama, kwamba mti wa mbuyu ulipasuka, nami nikazaliwa?" (uk.6)
Urudishaji wa maneno unaonekana katika matumizi ya neno 'leo' katika kauli ya mhusika Ashura. Mhusika huyu anatumia neno hilo kusisitiza. Anataka mwenzake aeleze kwa usahihi ni saa ngapi leo atamaliza kile anachozungumzia, kwa kuwa leo kuna masaa mengi. Mbuyu ni mmea. Njia ambayo mimea inazaliana ni tofauti na jinsi binadamu wanavyozaliwa. Katika tamko hili la RASHID, mmea huu umepewa sifa ya kujifungua kama mwanadamu. Ufasihi huu umetumiwa kuchochea tafakari miongoni mwa wakoloni waliokuwa wakiwatesa wakazi wa Zanzibar, wakiwasihi pia kuwaheshimu watu hawa Weusi ambao walizaliwa kama wanadamu wengine. Mulokozi (1996) anasema kwamba methali ni misemo mifupi iliyo na maana kubwa ndani yake. Katika fasihi simulizi ya Kiswahili, inadaiwa kwamba methali ni matokeo ya uzoefu wa maisha marefu waliopitia wazee, ndiyo maana mara nyingi huonekana kuwa za kweli zinaponukuliwa. Katika aina hii, kuna aina ndogo mbalimbali kama vile methali, vitendawili, misemo, na kauli. Methali zimetumika katika tamthilia hii iliyochaguliwa. Aina hii ya msemo ina sehemu mbili: sehemu ya kwanza inaelezea kitu, na sehemu ya pili inaelezea matokeo yake. Vile vile, katika ukurasa wa 3 mwandishi anasema, “Historia iliyoshikilia alizeti au waridi.” Uwezo wa kushika au kuhodhi kitu ni sifa inayomilikiwa na wanadamu. Binadamu hushika vitu kwa mikono yao. Katika kauli hii, mwandishi anapa uwezo wa kibinadamu historia, akidokeza kwamba inashikilia, inahifadhi, na kulinda mambo yenye thamani kubwa zaidi. Alizeti na waridi zimetumika kuonyesha mambo mazuri na ya kuvutia katika jamii. Katika tamathali hii ya usemi, maneno yaliyotumika yana maana tofauti kabisa na ile iliyokusudiwa. Inahitaji hadhira kufikiri kwa kina ili kutambua maana iliyokusudiwa. Mwandishi pia ametumia tamathali hii ya usemi katika tamthilia hii iliyochaguliwa. Kwa mfano,  
OKELLO: Shukrani ya punda ni teke. Watu watatu wanaorejelewa hapa na mhusika Okello wameshuka sana kiwango chao cha utendaji kazi. Imepunguzwa sana kiasi kwamba inaweza kulinganishwa na mwendo wa kobe, ambao unajulikana kuwa wa polepole sana, kwa maneno yasiyoweza kutamkwa. Kweli, hii ni kejeli au shere iliyolengwa kwa wapokeaji waliokusudiwa wa taarifa hii. Wanakumbushwa kufanya mambo haraka zaidi. 1.2.4 Ucheshi  
Hii ni tamathali ya usemi inayojulikana kwa kejeli kali (Senkoro 1981). Maneno yanayosikika ni tofauti kabisa na maana iliyokusudiwa. Mhusika mmoja, BIBI, ametumiwa na mwandishi kuwakilisha tamathali hii ya usemi katika tamthilia iliyochaguliwa.  
BIBI: ...Je, Mungu unayemwabudu amekuwa mjomba wako?... Huu msemo, "Umoja ni nguvu na utengano ni udhaifu," hutumiwa kuhamasisha umoja miongoni mwa wanajamii. Inasisitiza kwamba watu wanapaswa kushikamana pamoja katika chochote wanachonuia kufanya. Mwandishi anatumia methali hii kupitia kwa mhusika Okello anapowahamasisha vijana wenzake kwenda vitani ili kufanya mapinduzi na hatimaye kupata uhuru wa kweli katika nchi yao. Methali mbili za mwisho, "Shukrani ya punda ni teke" na "Subira hula kilichooza," zinaakisi majuto yanayompata mhusika mkuu wa tamthilia hii, John Okello. Mhusika mkuu huyu alitoa mchango mkubwa katika ukombozi wa nchi mbalimbali barani Afrika (ikiwa ni pamoja na Zanzibar), lakini hakukumbukwa popote. Kila mara alipomaliza mapambano ya ukombozi, alifukuzwa na kuishia gerezani. Mwandishi ametumia mbinu ya kejeli, akitamka methali kinyume; badala ya kusema “Subira hula kilichoiva,” aliandika “Subira hula kilichooza.” Yote haya yalikuwa kuelezea huzuni ya mhusika huyu, Okello. 1.2.7 Misemo  
Mhusika BIBI anauliza swali kwa watu wanaoonekana kumwabudu Mungu kila siku, lakini matendo yao yamejaa uonevu na ukosefu mkubwa wa haki. Matendo wanayofanya hayaonyeshi mafundisho ya Mwenyezi Mungu. Wanatesa watu, watumwa, na mtu yeyote mwingine anayevuka njia yao ambaye hana rangi sawa ya ngozi nao. Swali hili kwa kweli ni kejeli inayolenga wale wanaoonekana kumuogopa Mungu huku wakifanya matendo maovu. Mwandishi anasema, Mungu hadhihakiwi, hadanganywi, wala habeuliwi. Hizi ni kauli fupi ambazo jamii huzitumia kusisitiza ukweli wa jambo fulani. Inasemekana kwamba kauli kama hizo huunganisha dhana au mawazo mbalimbali kuwa wazo moja kwa lengo la kufikisha ujumbe uliokusudiwa. Ndani ya tamthilia iliyochaguliwa, Sadaka ya John Okello, mwandishi ametumia misemo mbalimbali. Kwa mfano;

Mwandishi wetu, Emmanuel Mbogo, ametumia lugha vyema sana katika ujenzi wa tamthilia hii. Kuanzia mwanzo hadi mwisho, msomaji anavutwa na kazi hii kila wakati. Ubunifu unaoelezwa na wanastrukturalisti katika nadharia unaonekana wazi katika kazi hii. Kwa kuwa lugha imetumiwa vyema, ujumbe uliokusudiwa bila shaka utawafikia hadhira. Endeleza ujuzi huu zaidi. 1.4 Hitimisho  
Fasihi ni tawi la sanaa linalotumia lugha ya maneno au maandishi kufikisha ujumbe kwa jamii. Ili ujumbe unaokusudiwa uwafikie wanajamii kwa ufanisi, ni muhimu kwa waandishi kutumia lugha kwa ubunifu katika kufikisha ujumbe huo kwa hadhira. Emmanuel Mbogo ni mkazi wa Tanzania bara, na tamthilia aliyoandika inawahusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Lafudhi zilizowekwa kwa wahusika wote katika kazi hii kwa kiasi kikubwa zinafanana na zile za wakazi wa visiwa hivyo. Waziri wa Kiarabu anapoongea, lugha humtambua. Mkazi wa Unguja anapoongea, lugha pia humtambua. Mtumwa kutoka bara, sehemu ya msafara wa watumwa kutoka Tabora, anapoongea, lugha pia humtambua. Wahusika wote wamepewa lugha inayolingana na majukumu yao. Vipengele vyote vilivyotumiwa vimeibua mada mbalimbali; mwandishi hakuvitumia kwa bahati mbaya. Sifa hizi za lugha zililenga kuibua mada tofauti ndani ya tamthilia hii. Hakika, misingi ya nadharia ya ujenzi

Introduction  
The use of language is one of the aspects found in the external structure of a literary work, that is, its form. Form encompasses all the essential elements used to shape a literary work, such as setting, characters, structure, style, and the title of the work/anthology, among others. In examining the use of language, critics focus on these elements: expressions, figures of speech, register, foreign languages, etc., depending on the critic’s objective. In this article, we explore the use of language in the play *John Okello’s Sacrifice* (2015).

discourses.source_txt:
1.1 The Theory of Formalism  
Schmitz (2007) and Carter (2006) have outlined several ideas of formalist theorists as follows: distinguishing between the use of ordinary language and literary language, they believed and emphasized that the concept of innovation or novelty is the main function of art, and they preferred literary criticism to have a scientific orientation; thus, they sought to establish scientific approaches in literature.  
According to the ideas of the formalists, all literary works utilize this theory because a work cannot be considered literary if it does not possess artistic qualities. These artistic qualities involve the construction of language elements that demonstrate the novelty of the work. Therefore, anyone who critiques any literary work based on the theory of Formalism will inevitably have to confront the issue of "novelty"—that is, the features that construct the use of language are unavoidable. The theory of Formalism is among the theories that analyze and explain the use of language in the disciplines of literature and linguistics. This theory originated from activists in two academic circles in Russia: on the one hand, the linguists of the Moscow Linguistics Circle, and on the other, the Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), both aiming to bring revolutions to linguistics and literary criticism (Schmitz, 2007).
discourses.translated_txt:
1.1 Nadharia ya Ufomalisti  
Schmitz (2007) na Carter (2006) wametoa maelezo ya mawazo mbalimbali ya wanadharia wa ufomalisti kama ifuatavyo: kwa kutofautisha kati ya matumizi ya lugha ya kawaida na lugha ya kisanaa, waliamini na kusisitiza kwamba dhana ya ubunifu au ubishara ndiyo kazi kuu ya sanaa, na walipendelea ukosoaji wa fasihi uwe na mwelekeo wa kisayansi; hivyo, walijitahidi kuweka mbinu za kisayansi katika fasihi.  
Kulingana na mawazo ya wanafalsafa wa ufomalisti, kazi zote za fasihi zinatumia nadharia hii kwa sababu kazi haiwezi kuchukuliwa kuwa ya kifasihi ikiwa haina sifa za kisanaa. Sifa hizi za kisanaa zinahusisha uundaji wa vipengele vya lugha vinavyoonyesha ubishara wa kazi. Kwa hiyo, yeyote anayekosoa kazi yoyote ya fasihi kwa mujibu wa nadharia ya Ufomalisti atakabiliana lazima na suala la "ubishara"—yani, sifa zinazojenga matumizi ya lugha haziwezi kuepukwa. Nadharia ya Ufomalisti ni miongoni mwa nadharia zinazochambua na kuelezea matumizi ya lugha katika taaluma za fasihi na isimu. Nadharia hii imetokana na wanaharakati kutoka mitaa miwili ya kitaaluma nchini Urusi: kwa upande mmoja, wanaisimu wa Moscow Linguistics Circle, na kwa upande mwingine, Society for the Study of Poetic Language (OPAYAZ), zote zikiwa na lengo la kuzua mapinduzi katika isimu na ukosoaji wa fasihi (Schmitz, 2007).

discourses.source_txt: In conclusion, the theory of Formalism has greatly contributed to the advancement and development of literary criticism. This contribution stems from the concept of innovation or novelty in literary works, the challenges and various debates it has sparked, which have generated diverse knowledge and ideas within the field of literature, as well as the emergence of other theories such as the theory of Modernism.

1.3 Comments and Recommendations  
Our author, Emmanuel Mbogo, has made excellent use of language in the construction of this play. From the beginning to the end, the reader is continually engaged with this work. The innovation described by structuralists in theory truly manifests itself in this work.

Mwandishi wetu, Emmanuel Mbogo, ametumia lugha vyema sana katika ujenzi wa tamthilia hii. Kuanzia mwanzo hadi mwisho, msomaji anavutwa na kazi hii kila wakati. Ubunifu unaoelezwa na wanastrukturalisti katika nadharia unaonekana wazi katika kazi hii.

1.4 Conclusion  
Literature is a branch of art that uses spoken or written language to convey a message to society. For the intended message to reach the community effectively, it is important for writers to use language creatively in delivering that message to the audience.

1.4 Hitimisho  
Fasihi ni tawi la sanaa linalotumia lugha ya maneno au maandishi kufikisha ujumbe kwa jamii. Ili ujumbe unaokusudiwa uwafikie wanajamii kwa ufanisi, ni muhimu kwa waandishi kutumia lugha kwa ubunifu katika kufikisha ujumbe huo kwa hadhira.

discourses.source_txt: Emmanuel Mbogo is a resident of mainland Tanzania, and the play he wrote concerns the people of Zanzibar (Unguja and Pemba). The accents given to all the characters in this work largely match those of the island inhabitants. When an Arab character speaks, the language identifies him. When a native of Unguja speaks, the language identifies him as well. When a slave from the mainland, part of a caravan of slaves from Tabora, speaks, the language also identifies him.
discourses.translated_txt: Emmanuel Mbogo ni mkazi wa Tanzania bara, na tamthilia aliyoandika inawahusu watu wa Zanzibar (Unguja na Pemba). Lafudhi zilizowekwa kwa wahusika wote katika kazi hii kwa kiasi kikubwa zinafanana na zile za wakazi wa visiwa hivyo. Waziri wa Kiarabu anapoongea, lugha humtambua. Mkazi wa Unguja anapoongea, lugha pia humtambua. Mtumwa kutoka bara, sehemu ya msafara wa watumwa kutoka Tabora, anapoongea, lugha pia humtambua.
